te: Ranong–Chumphon border security: border maps and help for local residents
se: The meeting considered security along the Ranong and Chumphon border with Myanmar. It heard information on border maps around Tha Sae District, the military’s work in the area and urgent proposals to help residents, took note of proposals from the Marine Task Force following a study visit, and approved the study visit report and the appointment of an academic adviser to the Committee
it: Security along the Ranong and Chumphon border with Myanmar: border map information and help for residents
Proposals of the marine task force arising from the committee's study visit
Subcommittees: veterans' affairs, cyber affairs, and the internal security seminar schedule
Study visit report, and academics and honorary advisers appointed

te: Briefing on the Volunteer Defence Corps' readiness for security threats and disasters
se: The meeting invited agency representatives to provide information on local public order and internal security work by the Volunteer Defence Corps, including staffing in each province, equipment and technology, training of reserve personnel to respond to security threats and major disasters, and welfare and pay, and approved holding the forum “Sustainable Internal Security Management”
it: Readiness of the Volunteer Defence Corps: staffing, equipment and technology, reserve personnel training, and welfare (agency representatives were invited to provide information)
Subcommittees: military affairs, cyber affairs and related work, and the forum “Sustainable Internal Security Management: Roles and Directions”
Invitation letters from other Senate committees

te: The unrest in the southern border provinces, and progress in using summoning powers under the 2025 law
se: The meeting considered the violence and unrest in the southern border provinces from October 2025 to June 2026, and resolved to hold press briefings in the Committee’s name, with any statement first approved by the meeting. It took note of progress under the Act on the Summoning Powers of Committees B.E. 2568 and the preparation of background information for the 17th AIPA Caucus meeting
it: Violence and unrest in the southern border provinces, October 2025–June 2026
Progress in implementing the Act on the Summoning Powers of Committees B.E. 2568
Background information for the 17th AIPA Caucus meeting, and sending summaries of meetings and visits to agencies
Parliament Radio and Television asks to interview the Subcommittee on Military Affairs

te: Draft military court law, border safety, and a resolution to use summoning powers under the 2025 law on the Ranong–Chumphon border
se: The meeting heard information on the draft Act on the Constitution of Military Courts (No. ..) B.E. .... and assigned the Military Affairs Subcommittee to prepare a report; considered improving safety along the border and supporting the work of the Volunteer Defence Corps, and Thailand–Myanmar border security in Ranong and Chumphon together with help for residents who farm there. The meeting resolved to confirm summoning persons to state facts or give views under the Act on the Summoning Powers of Committees B.E. 2568
it: Draft Military Court Constitution Act (No. ..) B.E. .... (information and views heard)
Strengthening safety and security along the border, and ways to support the work of the Volunteer Defence Corps
Thai–Myanmar border security in Ranong and Chumphon Provinces, together with help for residents who farm there
A petition asking for follow-up on a government agency's purchase of radio transceivers
Summary of the forum “22 years of the southern border provinces”

te: Agencies clarify the matter of Thai farmers along the Ranong border and the role of the Volunteer Defence Corps
se: The meeting heard about the role of the Volunteer Defence Corps in supporting security work, and invited agencies such as the Department of Treaties and Legal Affairs, the Royal Thai Survey Department, the Border Affairs Department, the 4th Army Area, the Thep Satri Task Force and Ranong Province to provide information on about 40 Thai households living and farming in the Thailand–Myanmar border area
it: Role and missions of the Volunteer Defence Corps in supporting security and public order
About 40 Thai households living and farming in the Thailand–Myanmar border area in Ranong Province (security, foreign affairs and provincial agencies were invited to provide information)
Proposal of Volunteer Defence Corps medals for committee members
12 honorary advisers to the committee appointed

te: Working group set up to study border bunkers, and follow-up on encroachment on state land in military areas
se: The meeting considered encroachment on state land in military areas, separating the matters within the Committee’s duties and powers; set up a working group to study and gather information on high-performance concrete bunkers to protect personnel and residents along the border; and took note of the subcommittees’ work, such as security study visits in the East and a visit to Chon Buri Province
it: Encroachment on state land in military areas
High-performance concrete bunkers to protect personnel and residents along the border
Subcommittees: an eastern study visit, technology for security, and 4 academic forums
4 honorary advisers to the committee appointed

te: Bunkers to protect border personnel, life insurance for soldiers, and a report on the MOU of 2000–2001
se: The meeting took note of the study report on the advantages and disadvantages of revoking the MOU of 2000 and the MOU of 2001 and Thailand–Cambodia border issues; considered ways to improve border safety with high-performance concrete bunkers to protect personnel and residents, life insurance for military personnel to support the morale of border personnel, and the insignia and medals of the Volunteer Defence Corps; and approved the report on the criteria for veterans’ benefits
it: Study report on the pros and cons of cancelling the MOU of 2000 and the MOU of 2001 and Thai–Cambodian border issues
Ways to improve border safety: high-performance concrete bunkers to protect the lives of personnel and residents
Life insurance for soldiers to support the morale of personnel on the border
Insignia and medals of the Volunteer Defence Corps
Subcommittee on Military Affairs: report on the criteria for veterans’ benefits, and the draft Act on the Constitution of Military Courts (No. ..) B.E. ....
11 honorary advisers to the committee appointed

te: Information heard on security cases and transnational crime, and policy proposals for the Middle East crisis
se: The meeting adjusted positions in the Committee (Mr. Virat Rakpan as Second Vice-Chair), took note of the resignation of Mr. Wirat Thummabumrong as a Committee member (effective 19 May 2026), invited the armed forces, the Royal Thai Police and related agencies to provide information on security and transnational crime cases involving foreign nationals found with weapons, and took note of policy recommendations for responding to the conflict in the Middle East
it: Changes to committee vice-chairs, and Mr. Wirat Thummabumrong's resignation as a committee member (effective 19 May 2026)
Security and transnational crime cases involving foreign nationals found with weapons (the armed forces, the Royal Thai Police and related agencies were invited to provide information)
Policy recommendations for the Middle East conflict crisis as it affects national security
Subcommittees: results of the discussion with the Minister of Defence and of the study of Thailand–Myanmar border security areas
10 honorary advisers to the committee appointed

te: Letters from local agencies in Surin and Ranong, the June–September framework, and following up the subcommittees' work
se: The meeting took note of letters to the Committee Chair from agencies, such as the Director of Internal Security Operations Region 4, the Governor of Surin Province (report on actions taken) and the Governor of Ranong Province (murky water in the Kraburi River), took note of the Chair’s discussions with border security agencies and the Ministry of Education, set the work framework for June–September 2026, and took note of the subcommittees’ reports
it: Letters from agencies: ISOC Region 4, the Governor of Surin and the Governor of Ranong (murky water in the Kraburi River)
The Committee Chair called on agencies to discuss strengthening border security, and held discussions with the Permanent Secretary of the Ministry of Education
Framework and approach of the committee and subcommittees, June–September 2026
Subcommittees: study visit postponed, cyber work reviewed, and results of the Thai–Myanmar border site visit
8 honorary advisers to the committee appointed

te: Position changes in the committee, and the effects of the Middle East situation on Thai energy and the economy
se: The meeting resolved to adjust positions in the Committee (Pol.Capt. Chalong Thongna as First Vice-Chair), adjusted positions in the subcommittees, approved Mr. Somboon Nunual as its representative on the Senate Ethics Committee, and invited energy and economic agencies such as the Ministry of Energy, the Bank of Thailand and the Federation of Thai Industries to provide information on the effects of the Middle East situation on national security
it: Changes to committee vice-chairs and subcommittee chairs/vice-chairs
Committee representative on the Senate Ethics Committee
The Middle East situation and its impact on Thailand’s energy and economic security (energy and economic agencies were invited to provide information)
Subcommittee on Military Affairs, and readiness for the study visit
10 honorary advisers to the committee appointed

te: The committee's budget, preparing the report to the Senate, and defence agencies on the security situation
se: The meeting assigned honorary advisers to join other committees’ seminars, took note of the 2026 budget summary and preparations to present study reports to the Senate in the 2026 ordinary session, invited the Permanent Secretary for Defence, the Chief of Defence Forces and the commanders of the armed forces or their representatives to provide information on responding to situations affecting security, and took note of the work plan of the Military Affairs Subcommittee
it: Facts on responding to situations affecting security and military missions (the Ministry of Defence, the Royal Thai Armed Forces Headquarters and the armed forces were invited to provide information)
Summary of the committee's 2026 budget, and preparing to present the report to the Senate
Field visit plan of the Military Affairs Subcommittee, 27–29 May 2026, and the Committee’s Action Plan

te: Election of the new committee chair (Mr. Somboon Nunual) and the framework for the second year
se: The meeting elected the Committee’s office holders, with Mr. Somboon Nunual elected as Committee Chair, together with the Vice-Chairs, Secretary and Spokesperson; adjusted subcommittee chairs and set the main work framework; heard information on encroachment on state land and damage to resources in the 4th Army Area; and resolved to cancel travel to bilateral meetings in the Russian Federation for fiscal year 2026
it: Election of the Chair, Vice-Chairs, Secretary and Spokesperson of the Committee (Mr. Somboon Nunual as Committee Chair), and changes to subcommittee chairs
Information on encroachment on state land and damage to natural resources in the 4th Army Area and ISOC Region 4
Performance reports of all 3 subcommittees (Military Affairs · Cyber, Technology, Weapons and Defence Industry · Holistic Security)
Study visit on eastern border security, and progress of the forum “22 years of the southern border provinces”
Travel to bilateral meetings in the Russian Federation, fiscal year 2026

te: Planning to invite agencies to clarify security matters, considering 6 complaints, and approving the subcommittee reports
se: The meeting took note of the reports presented to the Senate in 2025, approved a plan to invite agencies concerned to provide information on situations affecting security, considered 6 complaints and proposals sent to the Committee (some referred to the responsible agencies, some closed), and approved the subcommittees’ study reports, such as approaches to developing the armed forces’ personnel and deploying reserve personnel to support disaster relief
it: Plan to invite agencies concerned to give information on situations that affect security and military missions
6 complaints and proposals sent to the Committee (for example, a proposal to follow up the frigate project, and matters from the Senate Meets the People project)
Study report of the Military Affairs Subcommittee: developing the armed forces’ personnel, and a framework for deploying reserve personnel
Study report of the Subcommittee on Holistic Security, and the visit on residents’ land problems along the Thailand–Cambodia border
Forum “22 years of the southern border provinces” rescheduled, and progress on the strategic framework for emergency and disaster management

te: Trip to Russia called off in line with the Cabinet resolution, and following the effects of the Middle East conflict
se: In view of the fighting in the Middle East and the Cabinet resolution of 10 March 2026 to suspend travel, the meeting considered the trip to bilateral meetings in the Russian Federation, assigned the secretariat to follow and assess situations affecting security, prepared to present study reports to the Senate, approved holding the forum “22 Years of the Southern Border Provinces: Security Lessons towards a Safe and Lasting Peaceful Area”, and took note of the study visit to Nakhon Phanom and Khammouane Province, Lao PDR
it: Travel to bilateral meetings in the Russian Federation (Cabinet resolution of 10 March 2026 to call off the trip)
The conflict in the Middle East as it affects security and military missions
Preparing to present the committee's study report to the Senate
Academic forum “22 years of the southern border provinces: security lessons towards a safe and lasting peaceful area”
Results of the study visit to Nakhon Phanom Province, 9–11 February 2026, and Khammouane Province, Lao PDR

te: Proposals to develop the defence industry, a draft space affairs law, and the Middle East situation
se: The meeting assigned the Cyber Subcommittee to consider the Defence Industry Association’s proposals on developing the defence industry, took note of discussions on the draft Space Affairs Act, approved a study visit, and discussed the fighting in the Middle East that may affect Thailand
it: Proposals of the Defence Industry Association to develop the defence industry
Government agencies' responses to the Senate's observations
Subcommittees: results of the veterans forum, the draft Space Affairs Act, the study visit to boundary markers in Ranong, and the study report on the Internal Security Act
Study visit on military affairs and internal security
The fighting in the Middle East

te: Special allowances for personnel on the Thai–Cambodian border, and matters from border residents of Surin, Sa Kaeo and Satun
se: The meeting took note of the results of fact-finding on a petition about standing floodwater in Thani Subdistrict, Mueang Sukhothai District, took note of a proposal to allocate special allowances to personnel on duty in the Thailand–Cambodia border situation (July–December 2025), and referred 4 matters from the Senate Meets the People project to the agencies concerned, such as unidentified drones flying over the border in Kap Choeng District and residents’ land problems in Ta Phraya District
it: Results of fact-finding on grievances from 16 residents about standing floodwater in Thani Subdistrict, Mueang District, Sukhothai Province
Proposal to allocate special allowances to personnel on duty in the Thai–Cambodian border situation, July–December 2025

Matters from the Senate Meets the People project (4 items): unauthorised border crossings and unidentified drones along the border, Kap Choeng District, Surin Province; residents’ land problems, Ta Phraya District, Sa Kaeo Province; and opening hours of the Wang Prachan customs checkpoint, Satun Province
Cabinet resolution of 10 February 2026 relating to the committee's work
Performance reports of all 3 subcommittees (Military Affairs · Cyber, Technology, Weapons and Defence Industry · Holistic Security)
Site visit to study and follow up military affairs and internal security
